title: Americans have never had more of their money in stocks — not even in the dot-com bubble: Chart of the Day
summary:
Stocks made up 48.2% of Americans' financial assets in the second quarter, counting everything from brokerage accounts to 401(k)s, according to the Federal Reserve's latest Financial Accounts data.
It tops the 38.7% reached at the height of the dot-com mania and the 41% hit after the 2021 meme-stock frenzy.
Households hold about $74 trillion in stocks against roughly $20 trillion in bank deposits and money market funds — a record $3.65 in stocks for every dollar of cash.
When stocks rally and everything else sits still, stocks take up a bigger slice of the pie on their own.
A low share means plenty of money is left to move into stocks, usually at bargain prices.

title: Corgi could be dipping its tail into yet another business line: M&A
summary:
Corgi launched as an insurance startup, but it's been rapidly expanding into new businesses like thematic ETFs and 24/7 cafe/coworking spaces.
A job filing posted this month suggests it's now eyeing M&A investment banking.
The company, valued at $5 billion, is hiring for a "Managing Director, Investment Banking" role, according to the posting.
Unlike traditional investment banking jobs, which typically pair a hefty base salary with performance-based compensation, this job is "commission only, with no base salary."
Corgi was founded by Emily Yuan and Nico Laqua in 2024, offering a range of insurance products for startups.

title: Volvo plans to cut 2,500 jobs due to China's bruising pricing war
summary:
China's merciless car market is taking a bite out of Volvo.
On Friday, the Swedish luxury automaker said revenue in China fell by almost 50% over the past year.
The company said, like many legacy premium automakers, it's facing increasing "hypercompetition" from Chinese competitors.
Volvo plans to cut 2,500 jobs globally in response, it said, including roughly 2,000 in Sweden.
Volvo previously bet heavily on a rapid consumer transition to electric vehicles, aiming for an all-electric portfolio by 2030.
